title: What the decrypt method for AES/CTR/NoPadding ?

bodyText:
I have been looking through this PR and related issues/proposals,
but I can't find any reasoning about using Ctr64LE vs Ctr64BE as a "default" implementation of AES-ddd-CTR encryption/decryption.
I have a case where I want to encrypt generated messages in vector with "AES-128-CTR" encryption
and consume it from the java backend service. I use java's Cipher.getInstance("AES/CTR/NoPadding")
to decrypt message, however the deciphered payload does not match the payload that was encrypted in the vector.
I played a little with rust's aes and ctr crates and found that Ctr64BE::<aes::Aes128> matches with the java's "AES/CTR/NoPadding", but vector is using "Ctr64LE::<aes::Aes128>.
So my question is why vector using Ctr64LE? Is java's solution incorrect?
title: Endianness in AES-*-CTR encryption/decryption

bodyText:
Hi,
Description:
When attempting to generate a lockfile using Cargo for Vector Dev Version 0.33.0 and VRL Version 0.8.1, the process encounters an issue related to resolving the lalrpop dependency version. The error message indicates that it failed to select a suitable version for the requirement lalrpop = "^0.20.1". The relevant details of the error are as follows:
cargo generate-lockfile
    Updating git repository `https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector`
    Updating crates.io index
    Updating git repository `https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl`
error: failed to select a version for the requirement `lalrpop = "^0.20.1"`
candidate versions found which didn't match: 0.20.0, 0.19.12, 0.19.11, ...
location searched: crates.io index
required by package `vrl v0.8.0 (https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl?rev=v0.8.0#fb02bfdd)`
    ... which satisfies git dependency `vrl` of package `vrl-server v0.1.0 (/Users/parham/work/hamravesh9/pipelineoperator-client/images/vrl_validator)`
perhaps a crate was updated and forgotten to be re-vendored?


Steps to Reproduce:
Use Vector Dev Version 0.33.0.
Use VRL Version 0.8.1.
Run cargo generate-lockfile command.

Expected Behavior:
The cargo generate-lockfile command should complete successfully, resolving the lalrpop dependency to version ^0.20.1 without errors.
Actual Behavior:
The process encounters an error while attempting to select a version for the lalrpop requirement.
Additional Information:
my cargo.toml configuration:
[package]
name = "vrl-server"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
http = "0.2.9"

warp = "0.3.5"

vrl = { git = "https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl", rev = "v0.8.1" }
serde-wasm-bindgen = "0.5"
gloo-utils = { version = "0.1", features = ["serde"] }
getrandom = { version = "0.2", features = ["js"] }
vector-vrl-functions = { git = "https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector", tag = "v0.33.1"}
enrichment = { git = "https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector", tag = "v0.33.1"}
vector-common = { git = "https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector", tag = "v0.33.1"}

bodyText:
Hello,
I'm working with Vector and have a query regarding its regex capabilities in the remap language, specifically about compilation and caching. In my setup, I use various regex patterns within a remap transform, as shown below:
logFormat = .kubernetes.pod_annotations."my-company.io/log-format"
if logFormat == "format1" {
    pattern = r'...'
    . |= parse_regex!(.message, pattern)
} else if logFormat == "format2" {
    pattern = r'...'
    . |= parse_regex!(.message, pattern)
}

I plan to introduce more patterns and am concerned about potential performance impacts. My questions are:

Are regexes compiled and/or cached in Vector to enhance performance?
If regexes are not inherently cached, is there a way to precompile them or store them in a compiled format using an enrichment_table or similar feature?

Your insights would be greatly appreciated.
Best regards,
Peter
title: Regex performance question
